newsitem.title: INDIA: India allows foreigners to set up debt funds.
newsitem.headline: India allows foreigners to set up debt funds.

text.p: India's Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Friday that foreign financial institutions will be allowed to launch dedicated funds to invest in the country's debt market.
Chidambaram announced this as part of a series of fresh measures to boost to the country's capital markets.

"The Indian capital market suffers from a number of strucutural weaknesses which I intend to address systematically. But I am persuaded that there is urgent need to perk up market sentiment," Chidambaram told parliament.
"There are several FIIs that manage or intend to manage dedicated debt funds. It has been decided to allow FIIs to invest up to 100 percent of funds in debt instruments," Chidambaram said.
He said details on this will be announced by market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India.
